_comment: Marks on places (docs/ADVENTURES.md §5.19, §8.13; world/marks.py): what a settlement is going through, kept in Settlement.status. form: day (a day number: sacked, burned), name (tribute), or record (a dict with since, until...). label: the world map's word for it (with a colour: danger or warn). ages: {into, after [lo, hi] days from since} - when it passes into the next mark (into null: it is simply over); lasts [lo, hi]: the days a record lasts when it is given no until; a record with an until ends at it (siege is its war's; emptied and rebuilding are world/threats.py's, which mends the population). troubles: what you see walking in ({town}, {by}); moments: a thing seen in its streets; description: a line for a town's first description.

siege.label: under siege
troubles: <danger>{town} is under siege{by_part}.</> Soldiers' fires ring the walls, and food is dear inside them.
<danger>{town} is besieged{by_part}.</> The gates open only a crack, and the guards count every face.
<danger>The enemy's tents stand round {town}{by_part}.</> Inside, the streets are full of soldiers and short of bread.
moments: A sergeant counts sacks of grain into a cart and swears at the number.
Boys carry buckets of water up to the wall-walk.
Someone has chalked a tally of the days on the gatehouse.
description: The town is shut up behind its walls; the enemy's fires burn beyond them every night.

beset.label: beset
troubles: <danger>{town} is beset{by_part}.</> Nobody goes beyond the fences after dark, and the gates are barred at noon.
<danger>Something has {town} ringed round{by_part}.</> Fires are kept burning all night at every gap in the fence.
<danger>{town} lives behind barred doors{by_part}.</> The fields outside are not worked, and nobody says why aloud.
moments: Men stand at the gap in the fence with spears and lanterns, watching the dark.
A woman drives the last goats in through the gate and bars it behind them.
The bell is rung at noon to call the field-hands in, and they come running.
description: Its people keep behind their fences, and look out over them often.

sacked.label: sacked
troubles: <danger>{town} was sacked not long ago.</> Broken doors, fresh graves, and people who look at strangers with hate.
<danger>{town} has been sacked.</> The shutters are smashed, the wells fouled, and the market is ash.
<danger>Soldiers took {town} and did as soldiers do.</> Nobody here will tell you about it, and nobody needs to.
moments: A man nails a plank across a door that has no lock left to it.
Two women sort through a heap of broken pots for any that will still hold water.
Someone has scrubbed at a dark stain on the step until the stone is pale.
description: It was sacked not long ago, and has not yet forgotten it.

burning.label: burning
troubles: <danger>{town} is burning.</> The smoke is black and low, and people run past you with buckets and children.
<danger>Fire has taken {town}.</> Roofs fall in with a roar, and the heat comes down the street like a wall.
<danger>Half of {town} is alight.</> Nobody is guarding anything; everyone is carrying water or carrying the dead.
moments: A chain of people passes buckets from the well; the fire does not notice.
A roof falls in with a sound like a great breath let out.
A child sits in the road with a singed dog in her arms and does not cry.

burned.label: burned
troubles: <warn>Much of {town} has been burned.</> What is left huddles among the black beams.
<warn>{town} has burned.</> The ash is still soft underfoot, and the smell of it is in everything.
<warn>Where the houses of {town} stood there are black shells, open to the sky.</> People live in what is left.
moments: Crows walk in the ash of a house as if they own it.
A man sifts the ashes of his home through his fingers, looking for something small.
Someone has hung a black rag on a charred doorpost.
description: Fire went through it not long ago, and the black shells of houses stand open to the sky.

rebuilding.label: rebuilding
troubles: <warn>{town} is building itself again.</> New timber stands pale among the blackened beams.
<warn>Scaffolds stand over half of {town}.</> The hammering never stops while it is light.
<warn>{town} is coming back.</> There are new roofs, and new faces under them.
moments: A carpenter whistles on a scaffold, a mouthful of nails in his cheek.
A cart of new-cut stone grinds up the street.
Two neighbours argue over where one house ended and the next began.
description: It is being built again: new timber stands pale among the old black beams.

emptied.label: emptied
troubles: <danger>{town} is nearly empty.</> Doors stand open on empty rooms, and the few who stayed will not meet your eye.
<danger>Most of {town} has fled{by_part}.</> The houses are dark, and the dogs have gone wild in the lanes.
<danger>{town} has emptied{by_part}.</> Weeds already push up between the stones of the square.
moments: A door bangs in the wind, over and over, and nobody comes to shut it.
An old woman sweeps the step of a house with nobody in it.
Someone left a table laid for supper, and the mice have had it.
description: Most of its people have gone, and the empty houses wait for them.

plague.label: plague
troubles: <danger>Plague is in {town}.</> Doors are marked with chalk, and the dead-carts go by.
<danger>{town} is sick.</> Masked healers go from door to door, and the pyres smoke outside the walls.
<danger>There is plague in {town}.</> The streets are empty but for the carts, and the bells ring for the dead all day.
moments: A healer in a beaked mask knocks at a chalked door and waits.
The dead-cart creaks past, its driver with a cloth over his face.
Someone has hung bunches of rue over every window in the lane.
description: Sickness is in it, and the chalk marks on its doors say where.

famine.label: hungry
troubles: <warn>There is hunger here.</> Bread costs what meat should, and the children are thin.
<warn>{town} is hungry.</> A queue stands at the granary door from first light, and goes home with little.
<warn>The stalls of {town} are bare.</> What food there is goes for silver, and is watched while it is eaten.
moments: A queue stands at the granary door, and nobody in it speaks.
A boy is chased off from a bakery step, and comes straight back.
Someone is boiling nettles in a pot in the street.
description: It is a hungry place this year, and its people are thin.

raided.label: raided
troubles: <warn>{town} was raided days ago.</> The people are frightened and angry.
<warn>Raiders came to {town}{by_part}.</> Pens stand empty, and a burned barn still smokes.
<warn>{town} has been raided.</> Men with new spears stand at the gate, and do not much like your look.
moments: Men sharpen hay-forks by the well and talk low.
A woman counts her geese again, and again comes up short.
Someone has nailed a raider's shield to the gatepost, split.
description: It was raided not long ago, and keeps a closer watch on the road now.

tribute.label: paying tribute
troubles: <danger>{town} pays tribute to {by}.</> Cattle are driven up the mountain roads, and nobody looks at the sky for long.
<danger>{town} feeds {by}.</> Every month the best of its herds goes up the high road and does not come back.
<danger>{by} takes its due from {town}.</> The people here have learned to listen for wings.
moments: Herders drive a string of cattle out of the gate towards the hills, with their heads down.
A child points at a cloud, and her mother pulls her arm down hard.
The tithe-reeve chalks the count of the herds on a board by the gate.
description: It pays tribute to a dragon, and lives with one eye on the sky.

beast.label: beset by a beast
troubles: <danger>{by} has been at {town}.</> Doors are barred at dusk, and the dogs will not go out.
<danger>Something has killed near {town}{by_part}.</> Nobody walks the lanes alone, even at noon.
<danger>{town} is afraid{by_part}.</> Charms hang over every door, and the shepherds have brought the flocks in.
moments: A shepherd shows a torn fleece to anyone who will look.
Someone has hung a bundle of hawthorn over the gate.
Children play at hunting the beast, and the smallest has to be it.
description: A beast has been killing near it, and its doors are barred at dusk.

festival.label: celebrating
troubles: <good>{town} is celebrating.</> Garlands hang across the streets, and there is music in the square.
<good>It is a feast day in {town}.</> Stalls crowd the square, and nobody is working who can help it.
<good>{town} is in its best.</> Banners hang from the windows, and the inns are full to the doors.
moments: A fiddler plays for a ring of dancers who keep losing the step.
Children run under the garlands with ribbons in their hair.
A whole sheep turns on a spit in the square, and a crowd stands round it.
description: It is decked for a feast, garlands across its streets.

memorial.label: remembering
troubles: <dim>In the square of {town} stands a new memorial.</> Flowers are left at its foot.
<dim>{town} remembers what happened here.</> A stone in the square names the dead.
<dim>There is a memorial in {town} now.</> People touch it as they pass, without thinking.
moments: An old man stops at the memorial stone and takes off his hat.
Someone has left fresh flowers at the foot of the memorial.
A child traces the names cut in the memorial with one finger.
description: A memorial in its square names those it lost.
